reviews.text: I’ve been using Cal AI to track my calories and macros, and the photo scanning feature is really convenient. That said, the calorie estimates can be off for example, it labeled a small apple as 300 calories when it should be much lower. I also think the app is on the right track, but it really needs AI-driven custom meal plans to help you hit your goals. If it could suggest foods based on your leftover macros, that would be a game changer. As it stands, it’s pretty plain for what you’re paying, so I’d give it 3.5 stars instead of 5.

This is stupid, and frankly, just because you couldn’t keep the cost of your app, doesn’t mean you should still continue making that app. Money hungry pigs.

reviews.title: Expensive, Inaccurate, and Constantly Needs Correcting
reviews.text:
I paid for a yearly subscription to Cal AI and genuinely regret it. The entire point of using a nutrition-tracking app is to make tracking easier and more accurate, but I constantly have to double-check and correct this app.

Even when I scan the actual nutrition label, it frequently enters values that do not match the label right in front of me. I would estimate that 9 out of 10 products I scan require some kind of manual correction. At that point, what exactly is the AI saving me?

The Food Score is even more frustrating. The app repeatedly tells me that I am low on protein when my logged numbers clearly show that I have met or even exceeded the protein goal already set in the app. Foods can also receive poor scores because Cal AI fails to properly calculate things like fiber, sugar, and sodium. Worse, when I manually correct inaccurate nutrition information, the scoring system still does not seem to properly account for those corrections.

That makes the score feel arbitrary rather than useful. A nutrition app should not penalize a food because the app itself failed to capture its nutritional information correctly.

For a paid product—especially an annual subscription—basic nutrition-label scanning and macro calculations should be reliable. I should not have to audit nearly every entry against the package.

At this point, the only reason I continue using Cal AI is to maintain a rough idea of how many calories I am eating. I do not trust it enough for accurate macro or micronutrient tracking, and I definitely do not trust its Food Score.

I wish I had not purchased the yearly subscription. The concept is great, but the execution has been extremely disappointing.
